key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers with efficient charge extraction, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal perovskite tandems.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a potentially scalable route to stable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem optical performance using measured AgBiS2 absorption.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to passivate nanocrystals and increase usable film thickness.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing lead-halide perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
